records.mechanism: A makes permission to discuss the party conditional on revealing what B knows, using rank to avoid answering about personal involvement.
records.confusable: Ordinary evasiveness probes knowledge; this pair must turn B questions into applications A can approve or delimit.
records.comparison: The party alternative controls witnesses to a mishap; the keys alternative controls an account sent to a manager.
records.seedUse: Use D06-a party evidence and unanswered timing question, with S01 approval as the actual information-control tactic.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'll decide how we handle this. When you say you heard about the party, which part?

before.speaker: B
before.text: The cake went over the balcony. Was that before you left?

before.speaker: A
before.text: You can question the details after my decision. Who gave you the timing?

before.speaker: B
before.text: Nobody. Your brother says there's a video.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Have you watched it, or are we both relying on my brother?

after.speaker: A
after.text: The party report will come through me. What have you heard about the cake?

after.speaker: B
after.text: Someone dropped it over the balcony. Were you there?

after.speaker: A
after.text: You're permitted to establish who was there. Who else have you asked?

after.speaker: B
after.text: Nobody. Your brother says he filmed you.

after.speaker: A
after.text: You may send me that film before approaching any further witnesses. Have you actually seen my face in it?

records.reservation: A5 permission to send the film is prospective; it does not establish that B already possesses it.
records.firstDefect: No mandatory defect found on rereading the current five turns.

G1.evidence: A1 party report and B2 fallen cake establish a concrete inquiry; B4 names the brother as source rather than inventing confirmed guilt.

G2.evidence: A1 is collecting a party report; B2 knows a cake account; B4 has a brother claim, not necessarily the film.

G3.evidence: A1 asks what was heard; B2 reports the cake and asks whether A was present. A3 recasts B2 question as permission to investigate other witnesses. A3 asks who was consulted; B4 says nobody directly and introduces the brother footage claim. B4 filming claim causes A5 submission demand and a test of firsthand identification.

G4.evidence: B2 seeks a timeline and B4 reports a source; A3 and A5 restrict that inquiry without making B implausibly compliant.

G5.evidence: A1 controls the report, A3 licenses inquiry instead of answering, and A5 requires evidence submission while probing its contents.

G6.evidence: B4 moves from party rumor to purported footage of A, and A5 tightens control while avoiding admission.

format.evidence: A1, B2, A3, B4 and A5 satisfy the unchanged ABABA structure and 125-word pair limit.

before.text: I'll decide how we handle this. What did the manager say about the missing keys?

before.speaker: B

before.speaker: A
before.text: You can question the details after my decision. Is she asking everyone who locked up, or just me?

before.text: Did they say what I was doing, or only where I was?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I will handle the inquiry into the missing keys. What exactly did the manager tell you?

after.speaker: B
after.text: She thinks they're in the drain. Can I tell her you locked up?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll approve the wording after you've told me why she suspects the drain.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Someone saw you kneeling beside it.

after.speaker: A
after.text: You may quote that observation exactly. Did they see anything in my hands?

G4.evidence: B2 wants to inform the manager and B4 supplies relevant evidence, giving A a plausible report partner to control.

G6.evidence: B4 reveals proximity evidence, and A5 narrows authorized reporting while testing more incriminating detail.

after.text: She'll make me bake a whole pie.

before.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your rooftop wedding photo would look lovely. Try that staff-only door first.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'm the bride. They'll notice me.

before.speaker: A
before.text: You can question the details after my decision. They'll forgive you. I'll follow once you've explained the dress.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Then carry my train.

before.text: Gladly. I'll hold the very end, so if they object, only your train has followed you in.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I've approved a rooftop photograph for your wedding. You may lead us through that staff-only door.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Can you go first? They'll notice my dress.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Your request to change the order is declined. Bridal precedence stands. I'll follow once they've admired your dress.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Then carry my train.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Assistance is granted. I'll take the far end. You may make your entrance before any part of me crosses that threshold.

records.reservation: A claims authority over ceremonial order, not actual authority to repeal the staff restriction.

G4.evidence: B2 fears being noticed and B4 negotiates shared involvement, while A retains control of the terms.

G5.evidence: A1 grants entry precedence, A3 rejects changing order, and A5 approves assistance only in a form keeping B first across the rule.

G6.evidence: B4 tries to pull A into the entry; A5 grants help from the far end to preserve first exposure.

before.text: I'm labelling. We mustn't confuse it with tomorrow.

after.text: Reassignment denied. Use the wide-necked jar. I won't have you blaming the equipment.

after.text: Then what do I tell the curator when she sees it's empty?

after.text: Tell her you're still responsible for the contents. I'll label it 'One hour, awaiting delivery' and put your name beside 'supplier'.

cards.title: Say You Saw It Too
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit noticing the impossible detail before you reveal how much you believe it.
